subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.

requests.what: Neon light bar across the front of the cab roof: slim dark housing, six lamps alternating CYAN and MAGENTA, end brackets and a small amber beacon at each end.
Aggressive front grille on the cab nose: angled armoured slats in HULL_DARK, inner CYAN glow strips between them, a central emblem plate and a frame in STEEL.
Railgun turret detailing: capacitor coils along the barrels (CYAN rings), heat-sink fins, ammo feed box on the side, targeting sensor dome on top with a MAGENTA lens, and muzzle brakes.
Comms antenna array on the rear of the bed roof: a mast cluster of four whips of different heights, a dish, a flat phased-array panel and blinking AMBER tip lamps.
Left side missile pod (mirror on the right as a pair): 2x3 launch tubes in HULL_DARK with STEEL rims, WARN hazard stripe, mounting arms to the bed wall.
Underbody details: thick cable bundles, hydraulic lines in CYAN-sheathed hose, a driveshaft per axle, differential housings and a fuel tank on each side.
Rear cargo door: split armoured doors with hinge plates, a central locking bar, red tail light clusters, a hazard-striped bumper, and a faded licence plate with neon frame.
Cab armour kit: bolt-on armour plates over the doors, bullet-shield window slits frames, a bull bar with two amber fog lights, and side mirrors with cameras.
Night-city digital camo on the bed side panels (both hullSideL and hullSideR) in HULL, HULL_DARK and HULL_LIGHT, with a faded unit number and a small CYAN circuit-line motif.
Cab side panels: scuffed military paint in HULL with chipped edges to STEEL, a diagonal WARN stripe near the rear and a MAGENTA corporate emblem on the door.
Bed roof: panelled plating with rivets, hatch outlines, anti-slip grid and faint CYAN glyph markings.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a futuristic militarized 6x6 truck, roughly 8m long, 3m wide, 3.2m high, built efficiently from box parts without joints since it's a static model.

Mapping out the layout along the z-axis for the front bumper, cab, and cargo bed, plus three wheel axles with 0.65 radius, and positioning chassis rails and wheel offsets so the fenders cover them properly. Defining a color palette for hull, tires, rims, glass, and warning accents, then starting to build the chassis rails as the frame.

Still designing wheel geometry...

Adding windshield as a thin rotated box so it sits flush against the sloped roofline, working out the tilt angle needed to match the hood-to-roof geometry.

Still placing roof and hood armor plates...

Front details need a grille, bumper wedge, and glowing amber/cyan headlight strips near the nose. For the cargo bed, I'm sizing an armored container box behind the cab with a connecting dark gap piece to bridge cab and bed.

For the bed itself, I'm layering a lower hull and top slab with ribbed side panels, a rear ramp, and a turret ring mount on the roof holding a twin-barrel railgun pointed forward. I'll loop six vertical ribs per side for the armor plating and add wheel fender skirts, skipping rocket pods for now but planning rear lights, bumper, tow hooks, and exhaust stacks.

Then I'm adding fuel tanks, corner antennas, mirrors with arms, steps, and cyan underglow strips, plus a yellow-black hazard stripe pattern on the bumper made from six alternating boxes. I'm compiling a batch of eight additions and three texture requests, giving named parts like "hullSide," "cab," and "hood," and making sure side names stay unique like "hullSideL" to avoid naming collisions.

I'm pulling in a glow helper from the kit for the underglow effect, and sketching a box-creation helper function to simplify geometry calls, plus a mirror loop over left/right sides. I'm checking ground clearance math so the wheel bottoms sit exactly at zero and the overall vehicle height works out, then moving into writing the wheel geometry with tire and rim cylinder dimensions.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Checking fender and bed placements for clearance against wheel positions—adjusting bed height to 1.45-3.05 so it clears the wheel tops, and noting the cab bottom may need to shift to avoid intersecting the front wheels.

Still laying out the bed geometry...

Still placing panels...

I'm planning edits for the hull parts, thinking about how to apply a digital camo pattern to the hullSideL/hullSideR box geometry by quantizing cells based on position, since adding unit numbers or circuit motifs would be trickier with pure paint-based texturing.

I'm sketching a plan to draw a cyan circuit-line motif on side faces only using a condition on normal direction, plus a crude pixel-style "77" rendered as rectangles in a specific region. I also need to update the import statement to pull in paint, noise, and mix helpers, and adjust the box helper's color parameter type to accept either a string or a Paint object.

Writing camo noise logic...

I realize the panel inset piece sits on top and will hide most of the camo pattern underneath, since it's inset within the panel margins. I can't change the geometry now, so I'll just place the number decal and circuit details in the visible margin area instead.

Still mapping out digit strokes...

Adding circuit line details near the panel edge, then moving to the cab part's side paint logic for chipped steel edges using the outline coordinates and normals.

Adding the magenta diamond emblem with ring cutout on doors, plus scuff noise, and swapping the extrusion color to the cab paint for the main body part...

Now moving to the roof plates: paneling with seams and rivets on the top face, a hatch outline around the bed hatch, an anti-slip grid texture in a region near the bed, and faint cyan glyph markings.

Adding glyph hashing and vent/antiskid regions...

Still writing camo logic...
